NUNC PRO TUNC ORDER OF THE COMMISSION 
 
 Ind. Code ch . 8-1-26 provides t he procedure for the Indiana Utility Regulatory 
Commission’s Pipeline Safety Division (“Division”) to find violations of said chapter. Upon 
review of those findings, the Indiana Underground Plant Protection Advisory Committee 
(“Advisory Committee”) reviews those recommendations and recommends civil penalties in the 
Case.   
 
On February 23, 2022, the Commission upheld the finding of violation by the Pipeline 
Safety Division and approved the recommendation of the Advisory Committee  in Case Number 
24633. Since that time, it has been brought to the Commission ’s attention that the address of the 
damage location  was 7511 Middlefield Road and not 7535 Middlefield . Therefore, the 
Commission fi nds the clerical error made in the  damage location address fo r Case Number 
24633 shall be corrected to read 7511 Middlefield Road as reflected on the attached page.  
 
The Assistant General Counsel to the Division is directed to prepare and send notice to 
the parties advising them of the determination. 
 
Any approved civil penalties are due with in 90 days of the date of this Order unless 
payment arrangements are made with the Secretary of the Commission.   
 
Any approved trainings must be completed no later than 180 days from the date of this 
Order or the alternative civil penalty noted in the attached recommendation is due.   
 
IT IS SO ORDERED. 
 
HUSTON, FREEMAN, KREVDA, AND OBER CONCUR; ZIEGNER ABSENT: 
 
APPROVED: 
 
I hereby certify that the above is a true 
and correct copy of the Order as approved. 
 
 
      
Dana Kosco 
Secretary of the Commission

  Pursuant to India na Code chapte r 8 -1-26, the Pipeline Safety Division (“Division”)  of 
the Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission  (“Commission”) investigates excava tion damage 
cases and makes findings violations of said chapter. Upon review of those findings, the Indiana 
Underground Plant  Protection Advisory Committee (“Advisory Committee”) reviews those 
findings and recommends civil penalties in each case.   
 
Attached to this order are the cases received , with Division findings of violations and 
Advisory Committee recommendations, that are ripe for Commission action.   
 
The Commission hereby UPHOLDS the findings of violations by the Division and 
APPROVES the recommendations of the Advisory Committee as listed on the attached  pages. 
The Office of General Counsel is directed to prepare and send notice to the parties advising them 
of the determination. 
 
Civil penalties approved by the Commission are due within 90 days of the date of this 
Order unless payment arrangements are made with the Commission’s Office of General Counsel.   
 
Trainings approved by the Commission must be completed no later than 90 days from the 
date of this Order unless o therwise agreed in writing by the Commission’s O ffice of General 
Counsel for good cause shown . Failure to complete the training r esults in the alternative civil 
penalty noted in the attached recommendation becoming due.   
 
IT IS SO ORDERED. 
 
HUSTON, BENNETT, FREEMAN, VELETA, AND ZIEGNER CONCUR:

Dana Kosco

input.command:
cd /tmp/r2run-5bviqa_g/data/text; python3 -I - <<'E'
import re,glob,collections
c=collections.Counter()
for f in sorted(glob.glob('*.txt')):
    t=open(f).read()
    pages=t.split('=== page')[1:]
    n=sum(1 for p in pages[1:] if 'Case Number' in p)
    if n!=len(pages)-1: print('anom',f,n,len(pages)-1)
    y=2000+int(re.search(r'(\d\d)\.pdf|(\d\d)\.txt',f+'').group(0)[:2])
    c[y]+=n
print(sorted(c.items()),sum(c.values()))
E

Cases per year (by order date) are:

| Year | Cases |
|---|---|
| 2021 | 1,603 |
| 2022 | 2,672 |
| 2023 | 2,107 |
| 2024 | 1,897 |
| 2025 | 1,684 |

The total is 9,963 cases across the 58 orders, and **2022 has the most** with 2,672.

- **Method:** I counted the recommendation-form pages in each order's text, skipping the cover page. I took each order's year from its filename date, because the order date isn't in the extracted text.
- **Scan errors:** A few "finds the following violation(s)" lines were garbled by scanning (for example "fmds" and "f~llowing"). That is why I counted case-number pages instead of that phrase.
- **Nunc pro tunc order:** The 4/6/2022 nunc pro tunc order (`ord_PSDNPT_040622`) corrects the address on case 24633 and has one form. I counted it as one 2022 case. If you'd rather exclude it, 2022 drops to 2,671, which doesn't change the answer.
